chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:
I asked him about the urine of a boy that gets onto a garment, and he said: “Wash it.” I said: “What if I do not find its place?” He said: “Wash the entire garment.”

So this does not contradict what we have presented before, because it is possible that by his saying, “Wash it,” he meant: pour water over it; and it is also possible that he meant the urine of one who has eaten food.

key_terms.اغْسِلْهُ: wash it, the direct legal instruction given
key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: garment or cloth that has been soiled
key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: young boy, whose urine is the subject of the legal question
key_terms.الطَّعَامَ: food, indicating the possible distinction of a child who has begun eating food
key_terms.بَوْلِ: urine, the impurity being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.كُلَّهُ: all of it, indicating the entire garment should be washed
key_terms.مَكَانَهُ: its place, meaning the exact location of the impurity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a garment soiled by the urine of a young boy if the affected spot cannot be identified?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on urine from a young boy when it soils a garment. It states that the affected area should be washed, and if the exact place is unknown, the whole garment should be washed; the compiler then notes possible ways to reconcile this with earlier reports.
